clue.text: Drier and somewhat boring experience that's tedious

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a drag is something tiresome to sit through
-ish is a suffix meaning somewhat, now used as a word on its own

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a dull spell of tedium was fairly boring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drier' looks like an adjective about dullness but is the noun: a cloth for drying crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth used for wiping and drying washed crockery is a drier in the sense of a thing that dries.

clue.text: Note mocking the cost of the partnership?

parts.note: do is the first note of the sol-fa scale
wry humour is drily mocking

explanation.surface: A sarcastic note remarks on what a partnership costs.
explanation.walkthrough: The partnership is a marriage, and the question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride's family traditionally paid property to the groom, a price attached to the marriage partnership.

clue.text: Record-breaking hotel which is at the seaside

indicators.note: breaking into a piece means getting inside it

parts.note: a single is a record with one main track
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A seaside hotel has broken a record of some kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record-breaking' reads as one adjective, but it splits into the record and the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Shingle is the loose pebbles that cover many beaches, so it is found by the sea.

clue.text: Gripped and picked up like a gift

indicators.note: picked up as a radio picks up a signal, so heard rather than seen

parts.note: a gift is wrapped in paper

explanation.surface: Someone is gripped by, and picks up, something that looks like a present.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone completely absorbed in a story is held fast by it, gripped in the sense of enthralled.

clue.text: Hero taught to perform with stage manager

indicators.note: letters made to perform are put through their paces into a new order

explanation.surface: A hero has been coached to perform alongside the stage manager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stage manager' looks like a single theatre job; 'stage' is fodder and 'manager' alone is the definition. GARETH SOUTHGATE managed England's football team from 2016 to 2024.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the manager of the England men's football side, hailed a hero after the 2018 World Cup.

clue.text: Rock and roll fan after work briefly proved alluring

indicators.note: after puts the fan's letters following those for working briefly

parts.note: to temp is to do short-term office work
a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth devoted to rock and roll

explanation.surface: A rock and roll fan found something attractive after a short stint at work.
explanation.walkthrough: A Teddy boy (Ted) was a 1950s British youth in Edwardian-style suits who loved rock and roll.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that tempted a person drew them in, which is what being alluring means.

clue.text: Young reporter and undatable eccentric rang

parts.note: Tintin is the boy reporter of Hergé's comic books

indicators.note: eccentric means off-centre and odd, so the letters are put into a strange order

explanation.surface: A young journalist and an eccentric too odd to date both phoned.
explanation.definitionFit: Tintinnabulation is the ringing of bells, so to have tintinnabulated is to have rung.

clue.text: He has criminal still to uncover behind facial injury

parts.note: to moon is to show one's bare backside as a prank
a shiner is a black eye

explanation.surface: A criminal is still hiding behind something, with a black eye to show for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' is not an adverb but the noun: an apparatus for distilling spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who distils whisky illegally owns an unlawful still, the apparatus for making liquor.

clue.text: Luxury biography of female artist

parts.note: a biography is a written account of someone's life
Bridget Riley is a British painter known for op art

explanation.surface: A luxurious volume tells the life story of a woman painter.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a carefree existence of ease and comfort, a life of luxury.

clue.text: Not very bright setter does his best Russian

parts.note: dim means dull-witted or not bright
the setter refers to himself, giving I
to try is to do one's best

explanation.surface: The setter admits he is not clever but tries hard at Russian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Russian' looks like the language he is learning, but it defines a person with a Russian first name.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common Russian man's first name, so its bearer is typically a Russian.

clue.text: Dog handler with more in secure pens

indicators.note: pens means encloses, as a pen encloses animals

parts.note: to secure a prize is to win it
hipper means more fashionable, more in

explanation.surface: A dog handler with greater flair keeps his pens locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: A WHIPPER-IN is a huntsman's assistant who keeps the pack of hounds together.
explanation.definitionFit: This hunt servant manages the hounds, keeping strays in line with a whip.

clue.text: Lines I don't know in performance venue

parts.note: an ode is a poem, lines of verse
um is the noise of hesitant uncertainty

explanation.surface: An actor confesses not knowing their lines at a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece and Rome this was a roofed building for musical performances.

clue.text: Hindu ascetic American's greeting with grunt

parts.note: yo is an informal American hello
a grunt is US slang for an infantryman, a GI

explanation.surface: A holy man greets an American with a grunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grunt' looks like a noise but is slang for a common soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A practitioner of yoga who renounces worldly comforts is a Hindu holy man.

clue.text: Regime with a skint, corrupt parliament

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or perverted from its proper form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written; skint is British slang for having no money
a diet is a formal assembly, the parliament of Japan for one

explanation.surface: A regime alongside a broke and corrupt parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regime' suggests a government, fitting the parliament, but here it is a dietary regimen.
explanation.definitionFit: This low-carbohydrate eating plan is a regimen, which is a regime in the sense of a planned course of eating.

clue.text: Let go of key emergency facility

parts.note: to fire someone is to let them go from a job
Escape is a key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: Someone lets go of a key in an emergency.
explanation.definitionFit: An outside staircase that lets people leave a burning building is a safety facility for emergencies.

clue.text: Foremost of intellects in class?

indicators.note: in places the initial letter inside the word for class

parts.note: a genus is a class in biological classification

indicators.note: foremost of means the leading letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A question about the brightest mind in the class.
explanation.definitionFit: A person of exceptional brilliance is foremost among intellects, in a class of their own.

clue.text: Vote to imprison one, then check for innocence

indicators.note: imprisoning one piece means enclosing it within another

parts.note: nay is a vote against
I is the Roman numeral for one
to vet is to check thoroughly

explanation.surface: Voting to jail someone, then checking whether they are innocent.
explanation.definitionFit: Naivety is artless lack of worldly experience, a childlike innocence.

clue.text: Bill getting the water for Nancy's group still on stage

parts.note: a tab is a bill, as at a bar
Nancy is a French city, and the French for the water is l'eau

explanation.surface: A bill arrives for the water ordered by Nancy's group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nancy' looks like a woman's name but is the city in north-east France, signalling French.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a group of performers holding still in a pose on stage.

clue.text: Don't stay on the road — it's a bore

definitions.meaning: to leave the road you are on by taking a side road
something that kills interest or desire

explanation.surface: A driver is told to leave the road because it is dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a side road leaves the route; a thing that puts people off is also a dull let-down.

clue.text: Sportsman catching one more out there

indicators.note: catching means holding something inside

parts.note: a batter is a player at bat in baseball or cricket
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cricketer is caught out with one more ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching' and 'out' evoke dismissal in cricket; 'more out there' means crazier.
explanation.definitionFit: Batty means eccentric or mad, and 'out there' is slang for weird, so the comparative fits.

clue.text: Continue gambling? That's about right for Norman's neighbour

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: to bet on is to keep placing bets

explanation.surface: A gambler asks whether to keep betting, and whether that is right.
explanation.definitionFit: Brittany borders Normandy, so a native of Brittany is a neighbour of someone from Normandy.

clue.text: See 7
Short-changed minor name in finance

indicators.note: changed means altered, so these letters take a new order

parts.note: a minor is a child, someone under age

explanation.surface: A child was short-changed by a big name in finance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short-changed' reads as cheated but splits into fodder and its signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The family founded a famous European banking dynasty, a byword for wealth in finance.

clue.text: For fellow, this address might be used

definitions.text: For fellow, this address might be used

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for

explanation.surface: A note on how to address a college fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior academic or college fellow may be addressed by this short title for professor.

clue.text: Rank claimed by guard — it effectively rises

indicators.note: rises says the hidden letters are read backwards
claimed by the words means held within them, so the letters lie hidden across them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A rank is claimed by a guard who effectively rises to it.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Rank claimed' as the definition, but 'claimed by' signals the hidden letters; 'Rank' alone defines. In a down clue, 'rises' reads them upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Rank as an adjective means smelling foul, which is what a stinking thing is.

clue.text: Spades do some digging, moving easily

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for spades in card games
to pry is to dig into others' affairs

explanation.surface: Spades do some digging while the gardener moves with ease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spades' and 'digging' suggest gardening, but the digging is nosy inquiry.
explanation.definitionFit: Spry describes someone, especially older, who is nimble and moves with ease.

clue.text: European assents, one giving a spirited response?

definitions.meaning: the French and German words for yes, put together
a board for receiving messages from spirits at a seance

explanation.surface: Europeans saying yes, one of them responding with spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: The board's name joins the French and German words for yes; 'spirited' plays on spirits of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A seance board spells out replies supposedly sent by the spirits of the dead.

clue.text: Aid for flier getting good deal on gold hat

indicators.note: on in an across clue puts the good deal after the gold hat

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a topi is a sun helmet, a pith helmet
a lot is a good deal, a large amount

explanation.surface: A pilot gets a bargain on a golden hat.
explanation.definitionFit: An automatic system that flies an aircraft helps the pilot, an aid for whoever is flying.

clue.text: Islander with a sore bum getting into heavy metal

indicators.note: getting into puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron, a heavy metal

indicators.note: bum as an adjective means faulty or bad, so the letters are wrongly ordered

explanation.surface: An islander with a sore backside gets into heavy metal music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bum' looks like a backside but works as the adjective meaning bad.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Faroe Islands, in the North Atlantic, is an islander.

clue.text: Grass coloured bags with no tears

indicators.note: bags means grabs and holds, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: dyed means coloured
rye is a cereal grass

explanation.surface: Dyed grass is stuffed into bags without anyone crying.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who does not cry has eyes free of tears.
